questions.questionText: A farmer has 4 hectares of maize and applies fertiliser at 18 kg/ha. (a) Calculate the total fertiliser required. (b) State two factors that should be considered before applying fertiliser.
questions.explanation: Total fertiliser = 4 × 18 = 72 kg. Fertiliser decisions should consider soil and crop nutrient requirements and conditions at application.

questions.questionText: Describe how a farmer would take a representative soil sample from a cultivated field for laboratory analysis. State four precautions.
questions.explanation: Representative sampling reduces sampling error. Consistent depth, clean tools and exclusion of atypical areas improve reliability.

questions.questionText: Explain four factors that affect seed germination and state one practical way a farmer can manage each factor.
questions.explanation: Germination depends on viable seed plus suitable moisture, oxygen and temperature; management practices should create these conditions.

questions.questionText: Explain the difference between preventive and curative approaches to crop disease management. Give two examples of each.
questions.explanation: Integrated crop protection uses prevention first and targeted intervention where necessary.

questions.questionText: Describe four signs of good health in a farm animal and four signs that may indicate disease.
questions.explanation: Health assessment relies on comparing behaviour, intake, movement, respiration and appearance with normal signs for the species.

questions.questionText: Explain the functions of carbohydrates, proteins, minerals and vitamins in livestock diets.
questions.explanation: Balanced diets supply energy, building materials and regulatory nutrients.

questions.questionText: Explain why a vaccination programme is important in livestock production and distinguish vaccination from treatment.
questions.explanation: Vaccines are preventive biological preparations that stimulate immune responses; treatment addresses existing illness.

questions.questionText: Explain rotational grazing and give three advantages of using it on a farm.
questions.explanation: Rest periods allow pasture plants to recover and can improve utilisation and sustainability.

questions.questionText: List five routine maintenance operations for a tractor or farm machine and explain why maintenance is important.
questions.explanation: Preventive maintenance detects faults early and keeps machinery operating safely and efficiently.

questions.questionText: A farmer records sales of $8,400 and variable costs of $5,100 for an enterprise. Calculate the gross margin and explain what the result means.
questions.explanation: Gross margin is a useful short-term measure for comparing enterprises.

questions.questionText: Explain four factors a farmer should consider when choosing a market outlet for perishable produce.
questions.explanation: Perishable products require careful consideration of time, quality, price and transaction reliability.

questions.questionText: Explain how a farm inventory record can help management decisions. Give five examples of items that may be recorded.
questions.explanation: Accurate records support budgeting, stock control and planning.

questions.questionText: Describe five soil-conservation measures suitable for a sloping crop field and explain how each reduces erosion.
questions.explanation: Conservation practices reduce runoff velocity, protect the soil surface and improve infiltration.

questions.questionText: Explain the difference between weather and climate. Name four weather elements measured or observed for farm planning.
questions.explanation: Farm planning uses both short-term weather information and longer-term climate patterns.

questions.questionText: Compare sexual and asexual (vegetative) propagation in crop production. Give two advantages and two limitations of vegetative propagation.
questions.explanation: The choice depends on crop biology, disease status, desired uniformity and availability of planting material.

questions.questionText: Describe the characteristics, rainfall pattern, and suitable farming systems for Zimbabwe's Natural Regions II and V. [6 marks]
questions.explanation: Natural Region II receives 750–1,000 mm reliable summer rainfall, suited to intensive maize, tobacco, soya beans, wheat, and dairy/beef cattle [3 marks]. Natural Region V receives <450 mm erratic rainfall, suited to extensive cattle/goat ranching, wildlife (CAMPFIRE), and irrigated sugarcane in the Lowveld [3 marks].

questions.questionText:
(a) Distinguish between soil texture and soil structure. [2 marks]
(b) State three ways of improving clay soil structure for better crop growth. [3 marks]
questions.explanation:
(a) Soil texture is the relative proportion of sand, silt, and clay particles (permanent); soil structure is the arrangement of particles into aggregates/crumbs [2 marks].
(b) Add organic compost/kraal manure; apply agricultural lime (flocculates clay); avoid cultivating when wet and practise crop rotation with grasses [3 marks].

questions.questionText: Outline the lifecycle damage and two control methods each for (a) maize stalk borer [3 marks] and (b) aphids on cabbages [3 marks].
questions.explanation:
(a) Adult moths lay eggs under leaf sheaths; caterpillars bore into funnels/stems causing window-paning and dead-heart. Control: apply granular dipterex/karate into funnels at knee height; burn/bury old stover and rotate crops [3 marks].
(b) Sap-sucking insects deform leaves and transmit viruses. Control: spray dimethoate/malathion or encourage natural ladybird predators [3 marks].

questions.questionText:
A farmer plants 2 hectares of maize. Variable costs are: seed $120/ha, Compound D $180/ha, AN $140/ha, casual weeding $90/ha. Yield is 4.5 tonnes/ha sold at $300/tonne. Fixed costs total $450.
Calculate (a) Total Variable Costs, (b) Gross Margin, and (c) Net Farm Profit for the enterprise. [6 marks]
questions.explanation:
(a) Variable cost/ha = 120 + 180 + 140 + 90 = $530/ha. Total VC (2 ha) = $1,060 [2 marks].
(b) Gross Output = 2 × 4.5 × $300 = $2,700. Gross Margin = $2,700 - $1,060 = $1,640 [2 marks].
(c) Net Profit = Gross Margin - Fixed Costs = $1,640 - $450 = $1,190 [2 marks].

questions.questionText: Describe the functions of the four compartments of a ruminant stomach (rumen, reticulum, omasum, abomasum). [6 marks]
questions.explanation: Rumen: largest chamber; microbial fermentation breaks down cellulose and synthesises B-vitamins/amino acids [2]. Reticulum: honeycomb wall traps foreign hardware and passes food back for cud chewing [1]. Omasum: muscular folds squeeze/absorb water and volatile fatty acids [1]. Abomasum ("true stomach"): secretes HCl and pepsin to digest proteins normally [2].

questions.questionText:
(a) State four routine management practices carried out in broiler chicken production from day-old to 6 weeks. [4 marks]
(b) Give two biosecurity measures to protect the flock from Newcastle disease. [2 marks]
questions.explanation:
(a) Pre-heating brooder (~32–35°C); feeding starter crumbs then finisher mash with continuous clean water; strict litter cleanliness; vaccination schedule (e.g. Gumboro, Newcastle) [4 marks].
(b) Restrict visitors with disinfectant footbaths at doors; isolate new/sick birds and immunise flocks on schedule [2 marks].

questions.questionText: Explain the conservation advantages of Pfumvudza (conservation agriculture) over conventional deep mouldboard ploughing in semi-arid areas of Zimbabwe. [5 marks]
questions.explanation: Basin planting concentrates limited rainfall and fertiliser directly around root zones [2 marks]; permanent organic mulch suppresses weeds, cuts surface evaporation, and eliminates sheet erosion [2 marks]; minimum soil disturbance builds earthworm activity and organic carbon [1 mark].

questions.questionText: Describe how artificial insemination (AI) is carried out in dairy cattle and state three advantages over natural bull service. [5 marks]
questions.explanation: Semen from proven high-genetic-merit bulls is collected, frozen in liquid nitrogen straws, thawed, and deposited into the cow's cervix/uterus during standing heat using an AI gun [2 marks]. Advantages: eliminates cost/danger of keeping bulls; prevents venereal diseases; rapidly upgrades herd milk genetics across small farms [3 marks].

questions.questionText: Explain four precautions a farmer must observe when storing, mixing, and spraying agricultural pesticides. [4 marks]
questions.explanation: 1. Read label dilution instructions carefully. 2. Wear full PPE (overalls, rubber gloves, respirator mask, goggles). 3. Never spray in strong wind or eat/smoke while spraying. 4. Store locked away from food/children and dispose/triple-rinse empty containers safely [4 marks].

questions.questionText: Contrast vegetative propagation (e.g. sugarcane setts / sweet potato vines) with sexual seed propagation, giving two advantages and one disadvantage of vegetative propagation. [5 marks]
questions.explanation: Vegetative uses stems/tubers/cuttings producing genetically uniform clones rapidly; seed propagation uses fertilised gametes showing genetic variation [2 marks]. Advantages: preserves exact superior parent traits and yields earlier [2 marks]. Disadvantage: systemic viral diseases pass easily to offspring [1 mark].
